blueprint_concepts: Range of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x); maximum and minimum
english: Let $\overrightarrow{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{b}=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{c}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$. For $\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, let $\overrightarrow{r}(\theta)=\overrightarrow{c}+(\cos\theta)\,\overrightarrow{a}+(\sin\theta)\,\overrightarrow{b}$. Let $M$ and $m$ denote the maximum value and the minimum value, respectively, of $\left|\overrightarrow{r}(\theta)\right|^2$ for $\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Then the value of $M+m$ is ______.
hindi: माना $\overrightarrow{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{b}=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{c}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}$ हैं। $\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ के लिए माना $\overrightarrow{r}(\theta)=\overrightarrow{c}+(\cos\theta)\,\overrightarrow{a}+(\sin\theta)\,\overrightarrow{b}$ है। माना $\theta\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ के लिए $\left|\overrightarrow{r}(\theta)\right|^2$ के अधिकतम तथा न्यूनतम मान क्रमशः $M$ तथा $m$ हैं। तब $M+m$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Squaring and adding: the $\cos^2\theta$ and $\sin^2\theta$ terms give $36(\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta)=36$ and the $\sin\theta\cos\theta$ terms cancel ($16+16-32=0$)
$\theta-\varphi\in\left[-\varphi,\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\varphi\right]$; $\varphi>\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, so the minimum is at $\theta=0$: $m=65+36=101$ (at $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ the value is $113$)
solution_full: Adding: constants $29$; $\cos^2\theta$ and $\sin^2\theta$ both have coefficient $36$, giving $36$; the $\sin\theta\cos\theta$ terms cancel; linear terms $36\cos\theta+48\sin\theta$.
The overall range of $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta$ is $\left[-\sqrt{a^2+b^2},\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\right]$, but here $\theta$ is restricted, so the attained values must be checked.

Minimum: on $\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $\theta-\varphi$ runs over $\left[-\varphi,\dfrac{\pi}{2}-\varphi\right]$, which contains $0$ and has no point where cosine reaches $-1$; $\cos(\theta-\varphi)$ decreases as $|\theta-\varphi|$ grows, so the minimum is at the end farther from $\varphi$.
originality_note: New: a vector curve c + (cos t) a + (sin t) b in which a and b are hidden perpendicular vectors of equal length, so |r|^2 collapses to 65 + 36 cos t + 48 sin t; the restriction t in [0, pi/2] then makes the minimum an end-point value (way 4, hidden invariant). Closest known: 'maximum of a cos t + b sin t + c' as a plain trigonometric exercise. Different because: the expression must be built from vector components and the cancellation of cos^2, sin^2 and sin cos terms is the key, followed by an end-point check.

concept_use.Algebraic operations on a vector: Scalar multiples and the sum c + (cos t) a + (sin t) b give the components of r(t), whose squares are added to get |r|^2 = 65 + 36 cos t + 48 sin t.
concept_use.Range of a.sin(x) + b.cos(x); maximum an: 36 cos t + 48 sin t = 60 cos(t - phi) gives the maximum 125 at t = phi and, on the restricted interval, the minimum 101 at an end point.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, vector and point is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated the interval for theta twice (in the definition and for M, m) so the extremes are taken on [0, pi/2] only; M and m defined with 'respectively'. Changed: added the interval to the definition of M and m.
key_step: Cancellation in |r|^2 to 65 + 36 cos t + 48 sin t, then the restricted-interval extremes (interior maximum, end-point minimum).
justification: Two ideas linked: a vector expansion whose cross terms cancel, and the range of a cos + b sin on a restricted interval where the minimum is an end point (a typical trap of using 65 - 60). Numerical with no options; comparable to 2024-P1-Q3 (L3) in demand.
